A: "The Tipitaka (sometimes called Tripitaka) is the traditional term for the Buddhist scriptures. It is the version canonical to Theravada Buddhism and is generally referred to in English as the Pali Canon. The Tripitaka was composed between about 500 BCE to the start of the common era and was likely written down for the first time in the 1st century BCE. It contains the teachings of the Buddha and is divided into three \"baskets\" (pitaka): the Vinaya Pitaka (rules for monastic discipline), the Sutta Pitaka (discourses of the Buddha), and the Abhidhamma Pitaka (philosophical and doctrinal analysis)."
